advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reorder the guard so `coverage.get("read_set_recorded")` is checked before the store-reading `_declares_no_impact(...)` to preserve the no-read-set fast path.
evidence:
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:417 `if (
 not paths
 and not impact.poisoned
 and not _declares_no_impact(ticket_id, impact, repo_root=repo_root)
 and coverage.get("read_set_recorded")
 ):`
src/rebar/_lib_gates.py:118 `tracker = reads.tracker_dir(repo_root)` then `reads.ensure_fresh(tracker)` — _declares_no_impact does a store read on every call
The prior condition ordered the cheap `coverage.get("read_set_recorded")` as one of only two guards; a ticket with no recorded read-set short-circuited without any scope read.
advisory.finding: The new store-reading `_declares_no_impact()` guard is evaluated before the cheap `coverage.get("read_set_recorded")` check in the `and` chain, so every ticket with an empty pre-existing dependency set now triggers a file-impact scope read (get_file_impact_scope -> reads.ensure_fresh) even when no read-set was recorded — the common case that previously performed no such read and simply fell through to whole-HEAD.
scenarios: A container/leaf with empty declared+cited+inherited set and no recorded read-set (pre-agentic attestations, no fetch telemetry) — now incurs an extra tracker read per dependency_hashes call.
advisory.suggested_fix: Move `coverage.get("read_set_recorded")` ahead of `not _declares_no_impact(...)` in the `and` chain so the scope read only runs when a read-set was actually recorded.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the precondition count between ADR 0002 ('All four must hold') and manifest.py comment ('All three guards are load-bearing').
evidence: ADR: "All four must hold: the pre-existing dependency set ... is EMPTY; the container poison rule is NOT in effect; the ticket's own scope is UNDECLARED rather than an authenticated `none`; and a read-set was recorded."
manifest.py comment: "container that did not poison, for a ticket whose scope is UNDECLARED. All three guards\n    #   are load-bearing:"
advisory.finding: The ADR and the code comment disagree on the count of conditions for the same composition rule: the ADR says 'All four must hold' (empty set, not poisoned, own scope undeclared, read-set recorded), while the code comment says 'All three guards are load-bearing' — the same rule described with contradictory counts.
scenarios: A reader cross-referencing the ADR and the implementation comment to understand how many preconditions gate the scoping.
advisory.suggested_fix: Align the framing: either the code comment should say 'four preconditions' (including read-set recorded) or clarify that read-set-recorded is a precondition and only three are 'guards', matching the ADR wording.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for `_declares_no_impact`'s undeclared-container + `impact.all_none` arm (children all declare `none`, own scope undeclared) asserting the read-set scope is NOT applied.
evidence: ADR 0002 diff: 'An undeclared container whose live children all declare none, keep their exemption untouched.'

New test declares own scope none only: `rebar.declare_no_file_impact(ticket_id, "no code changes", ...)` (test_plan_review_attest_drift.py); it exercises `own_scope == 'none'`, not the `undeclared`+`all_none` branch.

ABSENCE: `test_a_poisoned_container_stays_at_the_whole_head_fail_safe` (line 372) drives `impact.poisoned=True` (a different guard); no test constructs live children all declaring `none` (impact.all_none=True) with an undeclared own scope.
advisory.finding: The new `_declares_no_impact` predicate's second arm — an UNDECLARED own scope with `impact.all_none` True (an undeclared container whose live children all declare none) — is a distinct behavioral branch introduced by this change but has no test. The only new test exercises the `own_scope == 'none'` arm via `declare_no_file_impact`; a regression dropping the `own_scope == 'undeclared' and impact.all_none` disjunct would go undetected.
scenarios: A container ticket with no own file_impact whose live children all declare file-scope none — the ADR-claimed exemption case.
